scope: parking (parking, stopping and standing a vehicle, and where each is not allowed)

vocabulary.definition: The person operating the vehicle that is being parked, stopped or stood, or is about to be.
To stop and leave a vehicle for any purpose other than loading or unloading passengers or merchandise; PARKED describes a vehicle in that state.
To stop a vehicle for any purpose other than loading or unloading passengers.
The portion of the road used by moving traffic, as distinct from the shoulder or the area off the road.
A portion of the roadway that connects sidewalks on opposite sides into a continuous path, or that has signs, lines or other markings for pedestrian crossing; it may be marked or unmarked.
A designated area, identified by specific signs, overhead yellow lights and pavement markings, that allows pedestrians to cross a road where there are no traffic lights.
A laminated permit issued to a person with a disability that entitles the vehicle in which the named person is travelling to park, stand or stop in designated disabled areas.
Parking a vehicle with its wheels parallel and next to the curb or side of the road.
Stopping by the side of the road for a short time, for example to check something outside the vehicle or to look at a map.
The vehicle's emergency flashers, which flash all turn signals at once.
Opening the driver's door with the right hand, which forces a shoulder check at the same time.

rules.title: Obey stopping, standing and parking signs
rules.when: signs say the DRIVER may not stop or limit stopping, standing or parking
rules.action: obey those signs
rules.statement: WHEN signs say the DRIVER may not stop or limit stopping, standing or parking, the DRIVER MUST obey those signs.

rules.title: Unposted parking by-laws
rules.when: choosing where to PARK
rules.action: be aware that not all parking by-laws are posted on signs
rules.statement: WHEN choosing where to PARK, the DRIVER SHOULD be aware that not all parking by-laws are posted on signs.
rules.note: Parking rules change from road to road and place to place.

rules.title: Shut down and lock after parking
rules.when: the vehicle has been PARKED
rules.action: turn off the ignition and the lights, remove the key and lock the door
rules.statement: WHEN the vehicle has been PARKED, the DRIVER MUST turn off the ignition and the lights, remove the key and lock the door.
rules.note: Reason given: to deter theft. Repeated in the parallel-parking and hill-parking steps.

rules.title: No children or animals left in a parked vehicle
rules.when: the vehicle has been PARKED
rules.action: leave children or animals in the vehicle
rules.statement: WHEN the vehicle has been PARKED, the DRIVER MUST NOT leave children or animals in the vehicle.

rules.title: Parking lights only for parking
rules.when: driving in low light
rules.action: use parking lights instead of headlights
rules.statement: WHEN driving in low light, the DRIVER MUST NOT use parking lights instead of headlights.
rules.note: The handbook says parking lights are only for parking.

rules.title: Turn off engine when parked over 10 seconds
rules.when: the vehicle is PARKED for more than 10 seconds
rules.action: turn off the vehicle
rules.statement: WHEN the vehicle is PARKED for more than 10 seconds, the DRIVER MUST turn off the vehicle.
rules.note: Given as a fuel-efficiency and emissions tip; reason given: engines warm up within 30 seconds even in cold weather.

rules.title: Never park on the travelled part of a road
rules.when: stopping to PARK
rules.action: PARK on the TRAVELLED PART OF THE ROAD
rules.statement: WHEN stopping to PARK, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK on the TRAVELLED PART OF THE ROAD.
rules.note: The parallel-park road-test task likewise says that where there is no curb, park off the travelled part of the road.

rules.title: Use the shoulder if you must stop
rules.when: the DRIVER must stop for some reason
rules.action: drive off the road onto the shoulder
rules.statement: WHEN the DRIVER must stop for some reason, the DRIVER MUST drive off the road onto the shoulder.

rules.title: No parking on curves, hills or without 125 m view
rules.when: the location is on a curve OR on a hill OR anywhere without a clear view for at least 125 metres in both directions
rules.action: PARK there
rules.statement: WHEN the location is on a curve OR on a hill OR anywhere without a clear view for at least 125 metres in both directions, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK there.

vague_terms.explanation: does not say what counts as an obstruction

rules.title: Do not block vehicles, sidewalks, crossings or entrances
rules.when: choosing where to PARK
rules.action: PARK where the vehicle will block a vehicle already PARKED, a sidewalk, a CROSSWALK, a pedestrian crossing or a road entrance
rules.statement: WHEN choosing where to PARK, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK where the vehicle will block a vehicle already PARKED, a sidewalk, a CROSSWALK, a pedestrian crossing or a road entrance.

rules.title: Fire hydrant: 3 metres
rules.when: within 3 metres of a fire hydrant
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN within 3 metres of a fire hydrant, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.

rules.title: Bridge: 100 metres
rules.when: on a bridge OR within 100 metres of a bridge
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN on a bridge OR within 100 metres of a bridge, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.

rules.title: Public entrances: 6 metres
rules.when: within 6 metres of a public entrance to a hotel, theatre or public hall AND that building is open to the public
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN within 6 metres of a public entrance to a hotel, theatre or public hall AND that building is open to the public, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.

rules.title: Intersection: 9 metres
rules.when: within 9 metres of an intersection
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN within 9 metres of an intersection, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.

rules.title: Signalized intersection: 15 metres
rules.when: within 15 metres of an intersection controlled by traffic lights
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN within 15 metres of an intersection controlled by traffic lights, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.

rules.title: Railway crossing: 15 metres
rules.when: within 15 metres of the nearest rail of a level railway crossing
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN within 15 metres of the nearest rail of a level railway crossing, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.

rules.title: Not in the way of traffic or snow clearing
rules.when: choosing where to PARK
rules.action: PARK where the vehicle will get in the way of traffic or snow clearing
rules.statement: WHEN choosing where to PARK, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK where the vehicle will get in the way of traffic or snow clearing.

rules.title: Watching an animal: pull completely off the road
rules.when: the DRIVER wishes to watch an animal
rules.action: first find a safe place to pull completely off the road and PARK, and not PARK on the shoulder of the road
rules.statement: WHEN the DRIVER wishes to watch an animal, the DRIVER MUST first find a safe place to pull completely off the road and PARK, and not PARK on the shoulder of the road.
rules.note: Reason given: other drivers may be distracted by the animal and hit the PARKED vehicle.

rules.title: Freeway trouble: never stop in driving lanes
rules.when: the vehicle has trouble on a freeway
rules.action: stop in the driving lanes
rules.statement: WHEN the vehicle has trouble on a freeway, the DRIVER MUST NOT stop in the driving lanes.
rules.note: The same block says to check mirrors, put on HAZARD LIGHTS, ease off the gas and pull over to the nearest shoulder as quickly as possible; see PARK-COND-03.

rules.title: Missed freeway exit: do not stop
rules.when: the DRIVER misses a freeway exit
rules.action: stop or reverse on the freeway
rules.statement: WHEN the DRIVER misses a freeway exit, the DRIVER MUST NOT stop or reverse on the freeway.
rules.note: The handbook says to take the next exit instead.

rules.title: Fog or whiteout: do not stop on the road
rules.when: driving in fog OR in blowing snow OR in a whiteout
rules.action: stop on the TRAVELLED PART OF THE ROAD
rules.statement: WHEN driving in fog OR in blowing snow OR in a whiteout, the DRIVER MUST NOT stop on the TRAVELLED PART OF THE ROAD.
rules.note: Reason given: the vehicle could become the first link in a chain-reaction collision. Stated for fog and for blowing snow and whiteouts.

rules.title: Permissive parking sign
rules.when: in the area between permissive parking signs (a green circle around a P)
rules.action: PARK there during the times posted
rules.statement: WHEN in the area between permissive parking signs (a green circle around a P), the DRIVER MAY ONLY PARK there during the times posted.
rules.note: The signs are used in pairs or groups; the example shows 30 min, 9 AM-6 PM, MON-FRI. MAY ONLY is read from 'during the times posted'.

rules.title: No stopping sign
rules.when: in the area between no-stopping signs
rules.action: stop the vehicle, even for a moment
rules.statement: WHEN in the area between no-stopping signs, the DRIVER MUST NOT stop the vehicle, even for a moment.
rules.note: Regulatory sign used in pairs or groups: a red circle with a slash over a stop-sign symbol, with arrows.

rules.title: No standing sign
rules.when: in the area between NO STANDING signs
rules.action: STAND
rules.statement: WHEN in the area between NO STANDING signs, the DRIVER MUST NOT STAND.
rules.note: Stopping while loading or unloading passengers is allowed. Regulatory sign used in pairs or groups.

rules.title: No parking sign
rules.when: in the area between no-parking signs
rules.action: PARK
rules.statement: WHEN in the area between no-parking signs, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK.
rules.note: Stopping to load or unload passengers or merchandise is allowed. Regulatory sign used in pairs or groups: a red circle with a slash over a P.

rules.title: Accessible parking spaces
rules.when: at a parking space designated for people with disabilities
rules.action: PARK there
rules.unless: an ACCESSIBLE PARKING PERMIT belonging to the DRIVER or to one of the passengers is displayed in the windshield
rules.statement: WHEN at a parking space designated for people with disabilities, the DRIVER MUST NOT PARK there, UNLESS an ACCESSIBLE PARKING PERMIT belonging to the DRIVER or to one of the passengers is displayed in the windshield.
rules.note: Worded as 'never' in the text; the regulatory sign (BY PERMIT ONLY) makes it a requirement. Misuse of a permit results in fines and revoked privileges. The permit may be displayed on the dashboard or the turned-down sun visor.

rules.title: Accessible pick-up and drop-off curb areas
rules.when: at a curb area reserved for picking up and dropping off passengers with disabilities
rules.action: STAND or stop there
rules.unless: the vehicle displays a valid ACCESSIBLE PARKING PERMIT belonging to the DRIVER or to one of the passengers AND the stop is to pick up or drop off passengers with disabilities
rules.statement: WHEN at a curb area reserved for picking up and dropping off passengers with disabilities, the DRIVER MUST NOT STAND or stop there, UNLESS the vehicle displays a valid ACCESSIBLE PARKING PERMIT belonging to the DRIVER or to one of the passengers AND the stop is to pick up or drop off passengers with disabilities.
rules.note: Combines the text with the NO STANDING / BY PERMIT ONLY sign.

rules.title: Permit entitles parking in designated areas
rules.when: the person named on an ACCESSIBLE PARKING PERMIT is travelling in the vehicle AND the permit is displayed on the dashboard or the turned-down sun visor
rules.action: PARK, STAND or stop in designated disabled parking, standing and stopping areas
rules.statement: WHEN the person named on an ACCESSIBLE PARKING PERMIT is travelling in the vehicle AND the permit is displayed on the dashboard or the turned-down sun visor, the DRIVER MAY PARK, STAND or stop in designated disabled parking, standing and stopping areas.
rules.note: The permit is issued to the person, not to a specific vehicle.

rules.title: Open doors only when safe
rules.when: the vehicle is PARKED
rules.action: open a door without first making sure it will not endanger any other person or vehicle or interfere with traffic
rules.statement: WHEN the vehicle is PARKED, the DRIVER MUST NOT open a door without first making sure it will not endanger any other person or vehicle or interfere with traffic.
rules.penalty: Three demerit points (improper opening of a vehicle door).

rules.title: Dutch reach
rules.when: opening the driver's door of a PARKED vehicle
rules.action: use the DUTCH REACH
rules.statement: WHEN opening the driver's door of a PARKED vehicle, the DRIVER SHOULD use the DUTCH REACH.
rules.note: Described as generally a good practice.

rules.title: Check traffic and cyclists before opening a door
rules.when: PARKED at the side of the roadway AND about to open a door
rules.action: check traffic, look behind, and check the mirrors and blind spots for passing cyclists, taking extra precautions not to open the door in a cyclist's path
rules.statement: WHEN PARKED at the side of the roadway AND about to open a door, the DRIVER MUST check traffic, look behind, and check the mirrors and blind spots for passing cyclists, taking extra precautions not to open the door in a cyclist's path.
rules.note: Cyclists often ride close to parked cars. Diagram 2-50 shows a door opened into a cyclist's path, marked as prohibited.

rules.title: Door next to traffic: minimum time
rules.when: a door of the PARKED vehicle must be opened next to traffic
rules.action: keep it open only long enough to load or unload passengers
rules.statement: WHEN a door of the PARKED vehicle must be opened next to traffic, the DRIVER MUST keep it open only long enough to load or unload passengers.

rules.title: Park parallel to the curb
rules.when: parking on a road where parking is allowed
rules.action: PARK parallel to the curb
rules.unless: signs say that vehicles should be PARKED at an angle
rules.statement: WHEN parking on a road where parking is allowed, the DRIVER MUST PARK parallel to the curb, UNLESS signs say that vehicles should be PARKED at an angle.

rules.title: Park on the right side
rules.when: parking on a road
rules.action: PARK on the right side of the road in the direction of traffic
rules.unless: the road is a one-way road
rules.statement: WHEN parking on a road, the DRIVER MUST PARK on the right side of the road in the direction of traffic, UNLESS the road is a one-way road.
rules.note: The one-way exception is taken from the next sentence in the same block (PARK-PAR-03).

rules.title: One-way roads: both sides
rules.when: on a one-way road where parking is allowed
rules.action: use PARALLEL PARKING on either side of the road
rules.statement: WHEN on a one-way road where parking is allowed, the DRIVER MAY use PARALLEL PARKING on either side of the road, UNLESS signs say otherwise.

rules.title: Choosing a parallel-parking space
rules.when: PARALLEL PARKING on the right-hand side of the road
rules.action: find a space about one and one-half times longer than the vehicle
rules.statement: WHEN PARALLEL PARKING on the right-hand side of the road, the DRIVER MUST find a space about one and one-half times longer than the vehicle.

rules.title: Check traffic and signal before pulling over to park
rules.when: about to pull over to PARALLEL PARK
rules.action: check the traffic beside and behind, signal the intention to pull over and stop, check the mirror before slowing down and check the blind spot before pulling into position
rules.statement: WHEN about to pull over to PARALLEL PARK, the DRIVER MUST check the traffic beside and behind, signal the intention to pull over and stop, check the mirror before slowing down and check the blind spot before pulling into position.
rules.note: Combines the handbook steps with the road-test checks. The road test adds: signal before slowing down unless vehicles are waiting to enter from side roads or driveways before the stopping point (see PARK-RS-02).

rules.title: Starting position for parallel parking
rules.when: getting into position to PARALLEL PARK
rules.action: drive alongside the vehicle ahead of the empty space, leaving about a metre and at least 60 centimetres between the vehicles, and stop when the rear bumper is in line with that vehicle
rules.statement: WHEN getting into position to PARALLEL PARK, the DRIVER MUST drive alongside the vehicle ahead of the empty space, leaving about a metre and at least 60 centimetres between the vehicles, and stop when the rear bumper is in line with that vehicle.
rules.note: The handbook says about a metre (11.30); the road-test task says at least 60 cm and to stop when completely in front of the empty space (29.240).

rules.title: Check before reversing into the space
rules.when: about to reverse into a parallel-parking space
rules.action: start reversing before looking all around the vehicle, checking the mirrors and both blind spots, and before the way is clear or traffic has stopped to let the DRIVER PARK
rules.statement: WHEN about to reverse into a parallel-parking space, the DRIVER MUST NOT start reversing before looking all around the vehicle, checking the mirrors and both blind spots, and before the way is clear or traffic has stopped to let the DRIVER PARK.

rules.title: Reversing into the space
rules.when: reversing into a parallel-parking space
rules.action: reverse slowly with the steering wheel turned fully toward the curb, straighten the wheels when the outside rear corner of the vehicle in front can be seen, turn the wheel fully toward the road to bring the vehicle in line with the curb, and drive forward to straighten if not parallel
rules.statement: WHEN reversing into a parallel-parking space, the DRIVER MUST reverse slowly with the steering wheel turned fully toward the curb, straighten the wheels when the outside rear corner of the vehicle in front can be seen, turn the wheel fully toward the road to bring the vehicle in line with the curb, and drive forward to straighten if not parallel.
rules.note: Diagram 2-52 shows the sequence.

rules.title: Final position in the space
rules.when: in a parallel-parking space
rules.action: move forward or backward to fit within the pavement markings or to leave room for the vehicles in front and behind to pull out, without hitting the curb or touching another vehicle
rules.statement: WHEN in a parallel-parking space, the DRIVER MUST move forward or backward to fit within the pavement markings or to leave room for the vehicles in front and behind to pull out, without hitting the curb or touching another vehicle.
rules.note: From the road-test task description.

rules.title: Secure the parked vehicle
rules.when: properly PARKED, including on a hill
rules.action: set the parking brake and move the gear selector into park, or shift into first or reverse gear if the vehicle has a manual transmission
rules.statement: WHEN properly PARKED, including on a hill, the DRIVER MUST set the parking brake and move the gear selector into park, or shift into first or reverse gear if the vehicle has a manual transmission.
rules.note: Road-test text allows a manual vehicle to be left in neutral if the engine is not turned off (see PARK-RS-08).

rules.title: Facing downhill
rules.when: parking facing downhill
rules.action: turn the front wheels towards the curb or right shoulder
rules.statement: WHEN parking facing downhill, the DRIVER MUST turn the front wheels towards the curb or right shoulder.
rules.note: Reason: keeps the vehicle from rolling into traffic if the brakes disengage. Diagram 2-53 A.

rules.title: Facing uphill with a curb
rules.when: parking facing uphill with a curb
rules.action: turn the steering wheel to the left so the wheels are turned towards the road
rules.statement: WHEN parking facing uphill with a curb, the DRIVER MUST turn the steering wheel to the left so the wheels are turned towards the road.
rules.note: Reason: the tires catch the curb if the vehicle rolls backward. Diagram 2-53 B.

rules.title: Facing uphill without a curb
rules.when: parking facing uphill without a curb
rules.action: turn the wheels sharply to the right
rules.statement: WHEN parking facing uphill without a curb, the DRIVER MUST turn the wheels sharply to the right.
rules.note: Reason: if the vehicle rolls it goes off the road rather than into traffic. Diagram 2-53 C.

rules.title: Checks before a roadside stop
rules.when: about to slow down for a ROADSIDE STOP
rules.action: check the mirrors and blind spot to see when the way is clear, and scan for signs to see whether the stop is legal
rules.statement: WHEN about to slow down for a ROADSIDE STOP, the DRIVER MUST check the mirrors and blind spot to see when the way is clear, and scan for signs to see whether the stop is legal.

vague_terms.explanation: the road test says a 150-metre gap in both directions is enough, but the handbook gives no required gap

rules.title: Signal timing for a roadside stop
rules.when: making a ROADSIDE STOP
rules.action: turn on the signal before slowing down
rules.unless: vehicles are waiting to enter the road from side roads or driveways between the vehicle and the stopping point, in which case wait until past those entrances before signalling
rules.statement: WHEN making a ROADSIDE STOP, the DRIVER MUST turn on the signal before slowing down, UNLESS vehicles are waiting to enter the road from side roads or driveways between the vehicle and the stopping point, in which case wait until past those entrances before signalling.
rules.note: Reason: so drivers will not think the vehicle is turning before the stopping point. The same rule applies before parallel parking and before a three-point turn.

rules.title: Roadside stop position
rules.when: making a ROADSIDE STOP where there is a curb
rules.action: steer to the side, steadily reducing speed, and stop parallel to the curb and not more than about 30 centimetres from it
rules.statement: WHEN making a ROADSIDE STOP where there is a curb, the DRIVER MUST steer to the side, steadily reducing speed, and stop parallel to the curb and not more than about 30 centimetres from it.
rules.note: 11.47 uses 'should not be more than about 30 cm'; the road test states it as a command. 11.47 also says curb or edge of the road.

rules.title: Roadside stop without a curb
rules.when: making a ROADSIDE STOP where there is no curb
rules.action: stop as far as possible off the TRAVELLED PART OF THE ROAD
rules.statement: WHEN making a ROADSIDE STOP where there is no curb, the DRIVER MUST stop as far as possible off the TRAVELLED PART OF THE ROAD.

rules.title: Do not block entrances or traffic
rules.when: making a ROADSIDE STOP
rules.action: stop where the vehicle will block an entrance or other traffic
rules.statement: WHEN making a ROADSIDE STOP, the DRIVER MUST NOT stop where the vehicle will block an entrance or other traffic.

rules.title: Hazard lights after a roadside stop
rules.when: stopped for a ROADSIDE STOP
rules.action: turn off the signal and turn on the HAZARD LIGHTS
rules.statement: WHEN stopped for a ROADSIDE STOP, the DRIVER MUST turn off the signal and turn on the HAZARD LIGHTS.

rules.title: Secure an automatic vehicle at a roadside stop
rules.when: stopped for a ROADSIDE STOP in a vehicle with an automatic transmission
rules.action: put the gear selector in park and set the parking brake
rules.statement: WHEN stopped for a ROADSIDE STOP in a vehicle with an automatic transmission, the DRIVER MUST put the gear selector in park and set the parking brake.

rules.title: Secure a manual vehicle at a roadside stop
rules.when: stopped for a ROADSIDE STOP in a vehicle with a manual transmission
rules.action: set the parking brake and shift into neutral if not turning off the engine, or into low or reverse if turning off the engine
rules.statement: WHEN stopped for a ROADSIDE STOP in a vehicle with a manual transmission, the DRIVER MUST set the parking brake and shift into neutral if not turning off the engine, or into low or reverse if turning off the engine.

rules.title: Roadside stop on a hill
rules.when: making a ROADSIDE STOP on a hill
rules.action: set the wheels against the curb in the appropriate direction to keep the vehicle from rolling
rules.statement: WHEN making a ROADSIDE STOP on a hill, the DRIVER MUST set the wheels against the curb in the appropriate direction to keep the vehicle from rolling.
rules.note: The appropriate directions are given in PARK-HILL-01 to PARK-HILL-03.

rules.title: Right blind spot before pulling over
rules.when: about to pull over for a ROADSIDE STOP AND traffic or pedestrians could overtake the vehicle on the right
rules.action: check the right blind spot just before pulling over
rules.statement: WHEN about to pull over for a ROADSIDE STOP AND traffic or pedestrians could overtake the vehicle on the right, the DRIVER MUST check the right blind spot just before pulling over.
rules.note: From the road-test task.

rules.title: Signal and check before leaving a parked position
rules.when: moving from a PARKED position
rules.action: signal, check for traffic, and pull out only when it is safe
rules.statement: WHEN moving from a PARKED position, the DRIVER MUST signal, check for traffic, and pull out only when it is safe.

rules.title: Prepare the vehicle to leave a roadside stop
rules.when: pulling out from a ROADSIDE STOP or a parking space
rules.action: release the parking brake and move the gear selector to drive or shift into first gear
rules.statement: WHEN pulling out from a ROADSIDE STOP or a parking space, the DRIVER MUST release the parking brake and move the gear selector to drive or shift into first gear.
rules.note: The road-test tasks also say to turn on the engine first.

rules.title: Hazard lights off, left signal on
rules.when: pulling out from a ROADSIDE STOP
rules.action: turn off the HAZARD LIGHTS and turn on the left-turn signal
rules.statement: WHEN pulling out from a ROADSIDE STOP, the DRIVER MUST turn off the HAZARD LIGHTS and turn on the left-turn signal.

rules.title: Mirror and blind-spot check before pulling away
rules.when: just before pulling away from a ROADSIDE STOP or a parking space
rules.action: check the mirrors and blind spot to make sure the way is clear of vehicles and cyclists
rules.statement: WHEN just before pulling away from a ROADSIDE STOP or a parking space, the DRIVER MUST check the mirrors and blind spot to make sure the way is clear of vehicles and cyclists.
rules.note: The road test specifies the left blind spot for a roadside stop.

rules.title: Accelerate smoothly to blend with traffic
rules.when: pulling out from a ROADSIDE STOP or a parking space
rules.action: return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around the vehicle, accelerating moderately in light traffic and more quickly in heavier traffic
rules.statement: WHEN pulling out from a ROADSIDE STOP or a parking space, the DRIVER MUST return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around the vehicle, accelerating moderately in light traffic and more quickly in heavier traffic.
rules.note: In a manual vehicle, shift gears as speed increases.

rules.title: Cancel the signal after pulling out
rules.when: the vehicle is back on the road after a ROADSIDE STOP or leaving a parking space
rules.action: turn off the left-turn signal
rules.statement: WHEN the vehicle is back on the road after a ROADSIDE STOP or leaving a parking space, the DRIVER MUST turn off the left-turn signal.

rules.title: Drowsy: pull off and park safely
rules.when: the DRIVER has any warning sign of serious drowsiness
rules.action: pull off the road, PARK in a safe, secure place such as a well-lit rest stop or truck stop on a busy road, lock the doors, roll up the windows and take a nap
rules.statement: WHEN the DRIVER has any warning sign of serious drowsiness, the DRIVER MUST pull off the road, PARK in a safe, secure place such as a well-lit rest stop or truck stop on a busy road, lock the doors, roll up the windows and take a nap.
rules.note: The warning signs are listed in 13.28-13.35.

rules.title: Dense fog or near-zero visibility: get off the road
rules.when: the fog is too dense to continue OR visibility is decreasing rapidly in fog or blowing snow
rules.action: pull completely off the road into a safe parking area if possible, and wait for conditions to improve
rules.statement: WHEN the fog is too dense to continue OR visibility is decreasing rapidly in fog or blowing snow, the DRIVER MUST pull completely off the road into a safe parking area if possible, and wait for conditions to improve.
rules.note: For whiteouts, 14.73 uses softer wording ('try to get off the road when visibility is near zero'); the stronger command wording from the fog passage and 14.81 is recorded.

rules.title: Lights when stopped off the road in fog
rules.when: stopped off the road because the fog is too dense to continue
rules.action: turn on the emergency flashers and keep the low-beam headlights on
rules.statement: WHEN stopped off the road because the fog is too dense to continue, the DRIVER MUST turn on the emergency flashers and keep the low-beam headlights on.

rules.title: Freeway trouble: pull onto the nearest shoulder
rules.when: there is a first sign of vehicle trouble on a freeway
rules.action: check the mirrors, put on the HAZARD LIGHTS, take the foot off the gas pedal and pull over to the nearest shoulder as quickly as possible
rules.statement: WHEN there is a first sign of vehicle trouble on a freeway, the DRIVER MUST check the mirrors, put on the HAZARD LIGHTS, take the foot off the gas pedal and pull over to the nearest shoulder as quickly as possible.
rules.note: The handbook says not to wait for the vehicle to stall on the freeway.
